To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we developed an ontology that models the sensory experience of a human subject in terms of a series of events, each of which is associated with a particular sense; (2) we developed a set of rules that can be used to determine the appropriate sense to be used when modeling a sensory experience, based on the nature of the stimulus;
we have developed a computational framework for the unambiguous characterization of sensory experiences.
the ontology is a useful tool to describe and compare different sensory experiences and to provide an overview of how sensory experiences can be described in a structured way.

the development of an ontology for the scientifically-based unambiguous characterization of sensory experiences, as well as its applications in the areas of health, wellness, and happiness.

The main takeaway from our work is that

a computable ontology of sensory science will enable a more complete understanding of the relationship between biological entities and the natural world, and will enable a more informed approach to the design of artificial systems that can be integrated into the biological system.

the development of a comprehensive and unambiguous knowledge base around the biological basis of sensory experiences will enable the development of a new class of applications that leverage our understanding of biological sensory systems to improve the health and well-being of humans.
the unambiguous characterization of biological entities and phenomena, along with the relationships between them is an essential prerequisite to understanding how the biological system works.
